result.title: Keep It CALM: Analyzing the Limits of Global Unsafety in Text-to-Image Generation
result.summary: Training-free safeguards for text-to-image generation often rely on a reusable safety signal, such as an unsafe direction or global toxic subspace, applied broadly across prompts. We provide a controlled geometric analysis of this global-unsafety assumption and reveal a consistent coverage-selectivity trade-off: compact unsafe subspaces fail to cover heterogeneous unsafe semantics, whereas broader aggregation increasingly distorts safety-adjacent benign prompts. Motivated by this finding, we propose CALM (Counterfactual Adaptive Local Modulation), a training-free safeguard that replaces uniform global removal with prompt-local counterfactual correction. Using matched unsafe-benign anchors, CALM routes each prompt to active unsafe categories, minimally edits only violating token representations toward the safe side, and suppresses positively aligned unsafe residual components. Across broad evaluation, CALM significantly improves unsafe content suppression while preserving benign utility, demonstrating that local counterfactual correction provides a more selective alternative to global unsafe signal removal.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文对文本到图像生成中「全局不安全子空间」这一免训练安全假设做受控几何分析，揭示覆盖度与选择性的权衡，并提出 CALM：用配对的安全-不安全锚点将提示路由到具体不安全类别，仅对违规 token 表示做局部反事实修正。
